title: Probabilistic load prober for p95 regression gating
creator: Lena Martinez
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, probabilistic load probing service that runs automatically during PRs to detect small but repeatable p95 latency regressions (and associated tokens/sec regressions) without requiring full-scale CI blasts.

Motivation: full-load CI benchmarks are expensive and slow. We need a middle path that provides statistically meaningful signals fast enough to gate PRs, while avoiding false positives caused by noisy CI hardware or unrelated infra events. The prober will sample a small fraction of production-like request shapes and run them in an isolated warm-path harness with controlled caching semantics.

Design summary:
- Sampling: reservoir-style probabilistic sampler that picks representative request traces from a maintained corpus (seeded from production telemetry and synthetic corner-case traces). Sampling rate is configurable by PR-level annotations and defaults to 0.5% of baseline traffic equivalent.
- Execution harness: short bursts (30-120s) executed in dedicated ephemeral pods with pinned GPU type and a warm KV cache pre-populated to approximate steady-state latencies. Each burst generates both generation requests (tokens/sec measurement) and end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99).
- Metrics & inference: compute p95 with bootstrap confidence intervals and maintain running baseline distributions using an exponentially-weighted window. Tokens/sec is measured using token-completion-rate over the same burst windows. Detection uses a Bayesian change point test (posterior probability) combined with effect-size filter: require both posterior_prob > 0.995 and relative p95 increase >= 7% OR absolute tokens/sec drop >= 6% to consider a failing signal.
- Gating policy: a PR is flagged for performance review if two consecutive prober runs (on different CI agents) produce failing signals. Automated block only for P0/P1 branches; otherwise, label PR with "perf-review" and post summary. We provide an opt-out label for noisy experimental branches.
- Baselines & maintenance: keep per-model/per-sequence-length baseline buckets. Baselines are updated via controlled rolling baselining job that runs nightly and requires stable canary windows. Baseline versioning stored in S3 with semantic version tags to attribute drifts to model or infra changes.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Noise: short bursts are more cost-efficient but higher variance than long-load tests. We mitigate with bootstrap CIs, multiple independent runs, and sampling orthogonality (mix of synthetic and captured traces).
- Cache effects: warm vs cold cache drastically alters p95. We standardize on "warm-path" by pre-warming KV caches and documenting when a probe intentionally exercises cold-cache behavior.
- Cost vs sensitivity: tuning the sampling rate and burst length is a knob; we default for a balance but expose controls for repo owners.

Operational hooks:
- Dashboard: perf-prober dashboard (per-model, per-base, run-level diff with CIs) and historical run replay.
- Alerts: create low-noise perf-alerts for persistent baseline shifts.
- PR integration: bot comment with short summary, link to dashboard, and a one-line verdict (OK / REVIEW / FAIL).

Next steps:
1) Implement sampler library and local harness prototype (Marco).
2) Add bootstrap CI job and gating integration (Lena + CI infra).
3) Run cross-team trial on 3 models for 2 weeks and iterate thresholds.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Marco Chen: Prototype harness running locally. Verified bootstrap CI job can schedule ephemeral pin-type pods. Observed expected variance on 30s bursts; added bootstrap CI to compute 95% CI for p95.

2026-03-02 - Lena Martinez: Experimented with sampling corpus (prod traces + synthetic). Reservoir sampler implemented; initial runs showed a consistent ~3% p95 variance between hosts. Decided to require two independent failing runs before gating.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Aisha Kapoor): UX for PR bot comment approved. PM requested explicit opt-out label and a succinct one-line verdict for PR reviewers.

2026-03-09 - Performance team (internal): Ran three-day trial across models 'redwood-small', 'rw-13b' and 'search-embed'. Detected a 9% p95 regression on rw-13b tied to a kernel change; reproduced locally and rolled back kernel selection in canary. Evidence logged in internal incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-09-kernel-latency-spike
